title: Zeros and Factored Form
short: The zeros of a(x − p)(x − q) are p and q, where the graph meets the x-axis.
trouble: Students read the zeros of (x + 4)(x − 1) as 4 and −1.

blocks.html: The form $y = a(x - p)(x - q)$ is called factored form (or intercept form). Thanks to the zero product property, it shows where the parabola crosses the $x$-axis.

At $x = p$ the first factor is $0$, so $y = 0$; the same happens at $x = q$. These are the zeros of the function and the $x$-intercepts of the graph, and no other input gives $0$. By symmetry, the axis of the parabola lies halfway between the zeros, at $x = \frac{p + q}{2}$, so the vertex is there too. The number $a$ still controls direction and width.

blocks.name: parabola
blocks.cap: $y = -(x + 2)(x - 4)$: zeros at $-2$ and $4$, axis halfway at $x = 1$. Move $r$ and $s$ to move the zeros.

blocks.html: $y = a(x - p)(x - q)$ has zeros $p$ and $q$ (opposite in sign to the numbers in the factors), axis of symmetry $x = \frac{p + q}{2}$, and opens up when $a > 0$.

blocks.title: Zeros and vertex
blocks.q: Find the zeros and the vertex of $y = 2(x + 1)(x - 5)$.

blocks.title: Write from the zeros
blocks.q: A parabola has zeros $-3$ and $1$ and $y$-intercept $6$. Write it in factored form.

blocks.html: Reading the zeros of $(x + 4)(x - 1)$ as $4$ and $-1$. A zero makes a factor equal $0$: $x + 4 = 0$ at $x = -4$. Check by substituting: $(-4 + 4)(-4 - 1) = 0$, but $(4 + 4)(4 - 1) = 24$.
